items.sentence: Overlapping microscopic scales coat its wings, producing colors through pigments and light-reflecting structures.
Two pairs of wings attach to its thorax, while three pairs of jointed legs support its body.
Long, club-tipped antennae extend from its head and help detect odors and orient during flight.
A tightly coiled feeding tube lies beneath its head and can uncoil to reach liquid food.
It samples chemicals with sensors on its feet, helping determine whether a leaf is suitable for laying eggs.
While feeding, it uncoils its slender tube to draw nectar from flowers.
Many species bask with wings open or closed, adjusting their posture to absorb warmth from sunlight.
Some populations travel long distances seasonally, following routes that can span several generations.
Adults are commonly found in sunny gardens, meadows, and woodland clearings where flowering plants provide nectar.
Many species spend their early lives on particular host plants, so their presence depends on local vegetation.
In tropical forests, species occupy different canopy layers, with some living high above the forest floor.
Cold winters may be passed as eggs, larvae, pupae, or adults, depending on the species.
While visiting flowers for nectar, it can transfer pollen between blooms and contribute to plant reproduction.
Its eggs and larvae provide food for birds, spiders, and other predators in terrestrial food webs.
Because many species respond quickly to habitat changes, their populations can help monitor ecosystem condition.
Bright wing patterns can startle predators or signal an unpleasant taste in species that store defensive chemicals.
